meta.title: Magnetic coupling calculator, Addendum A data: grades (A6), part mapping, materials (A5)
meta.status: PENDING USER DECISIONS (report section 8). Every 'value' is the recommended option; items with a 'decision' block carry every option.
resolution_rule: 1 condition match (values at another condition are alternates)
2 vendor minimum for guaranteed properties (yield; Br, Hcj, Hcb, BHmax), typical kept as typ
3 primary over secondary (manufacturer > distributor/aggregator; resin producer > stock-shape converter; grade-specific sheet > family average; part vendor governs its own parts)
4 otherwise a user decision, conservative option recommended
user decision D1 (K&J minimum basis for NdFeB) overrides rule 3 for NdFeB grade records (decision 1 confirms the extension)
meta.library_vs_workbook: The library carries the sourced value. Where the engine has a workbook number that differs, the engine default profile keeps the workbook number (workbook_default / workbook_defaults); a sourced value reaches the engine only through a registered deviation.

materials.iacs_to_S_per_m: sigma = pct/100 x 58.0e6 S/m (100 % IACS = 58e6 S/m at 20 C; Wikipedia, tier 3: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Annealed_Copper_Standard)
materials.ksi_and_Msi: x 6.894757 (MPa per ksi, GPa per Msi)
materials.chart_read_mu_r: mu_r = B / (mu0 H) with H in Oe: mu0 H [T] = 1e-4 x H[Oe]; H = 140 Oe -> 0.014 T

grade_discrepancies_from_research.what: Engine beta(Hcj) = -0.005 /C (-0.50 %/C, 'effective 20-150 C') against Arnold N42SH -0.55 %/C measured 20-150 C (catalog -0.549).
grade_discrepancies_from_research.effect: At 150 C the engine keeps 1 - 0.0050*130 = 0.350 of the 20 C Hcj; Arnold's coefficient keeps 1 - 0.0055*130 = 0.285, so the engine Hcj(150 C) is 23 percent higher (non-conservative). The audit already noted the coefficient (docs/analyses/2026-09-29-magcoupling-math-audit.md line 436).

grade_discrepancies_from_research.what: Engine hcj20 = 1592 kA/m matches Arnold N42SH HcJ min (20,000 Oe = 1,592 kA/m) and K&J 'Hci > 20 kOe' (1591.5 kA/m); engine alpha_Br = -0.0012 /C matches Arnold -0.12 %/C (20-150 C).
grade_discrepancies_from_research.effect: Consistent for N42SH. The same 1592 kA/m applied to a N42 part over-states its Hcj by a factor 1.67 (N42 min 955 kA/m Arnold, 954.9 kA/m K&J); that is the A6 correctness fix.

grade_discrepancies_from_research.what: SuperMagnetMan product pages show Max Working Temp 60 C for M5044, M5045 and M5026; library.py stores 80, 100, 80. M5045's spec grid says 'Neodymium 50' while its title says N50M. M5045's grid length is 0.256 in (6.50 mm) against 6.56 mm in the title and library.
grade_discrepancies_from_research.effect: Not resolved here. library.py tmax_C (80, 100, 80) exceeds the vendor-stated working temperature (60) for all three arc parts.

grade_discrepancies_from_research.what: Library Br = 1.42 T for N50/N50M is not a published minimum: K&J N50 and N50M min 1.41 T; Arnold N50 min 1.39, nominal 1.425; Arnold N50M min 1.39, nominal 1.415.

grade_discrepancies_from_research.what: Vendors disagree on the minimum: N42SH Br K&J 1.30 vs Arnold 1.28 T; N42 1.30 vs 1.28; N52 1.45 vs 1.42; N42SH BHmax min K&J 40 MGOe (318.3 kJ/m3) vs Arnold 39 MGOe (310).

grade_discrepancies_from_research.what: Coefficient ranges are short: N52 20-60 C; N35, N42, N48, N50 20-80 C; N42M 20-100 C; N42H 20-120 C; N42SH 20-150 C; N38UH 20-180 C; N35EH 20-200 C; N33AH 20-220 C. Outside them the linear coefficient is extrapolation; TN 0303 says the change is non-linear.

grade_discrepancies_from_research.what: Eclipse SmCo datasheet prints Hci (kA/m) as >1433, >1433, >1434, >1435, >1436 for SmCo22, 24, 26, 28, 30 while its kOe column reads >18, >18, >19, >20, >21. The kOe column is used (converted), the kA/m column is not.

grade_discrepancies_from_research.what: Arnold's nominal value falls outside K&J's min-max window for some grades because the two vendors define the grade windows differently: N35 BHmax: Arnold nominal 283 kJ/m3 vs K&J 262.6-278.5; N42M BHmax: Arnold nominal 338 kJ/m3 vs K&J 318.3-334.2; N38UH BHmax: Arnold nominal 307 kJ/m3 vs K&J 286.5-302.4; N35EH BHmax: Arnold nominal 279 kJ/m3 vs K&J 262.6-278.5; N33AH BHmax: Arnold nominal 231 kJ/m3 vs K&J 246.7-262.6.
grade_discrepancies_from_research.effect: This is why typ is left null on the K&J-based records and Arnold's min/nominal/max sit under alternatives. N33AH is the largest split: K&J 31-33 MGOe with Br 1.14-1.17 T, Arnold nominal 29 MGOe with Br 1.14 T nominal (min 1.11).

grade_open_gaps: Recoil permeability: no per-grade value published by any source found. Class-level 1.05 (K&J for all NdFeB; Arnold 2006 for sintered NdFeB, SmCo and ferrite). Bonded NdFeB: Arnold gives only a range 1.1-1.7, so mu_rec is null for the bonded grade.

Typical values: K&J publishes ranges only, so typ is null on the K&J-based NdFeB records; Arnold's min/nominal/max are under alternatives and in section 1b. Hcj has no typical or maximum in either vendor's sheet.

Hard ferrite Y30: no manufacturer datasheet was retrievable (Arnold ceramic sheets returned nothing; TDK blocked with HTTP 403); values come from distributors (Eclipse, Hyab, Alliance). Eclipse prints no temperature range for its ferrite coefficients; the 20-120 C range is from Arnold TN 0303 for Ferrite 8, not Y30.

Bonded NdFeB: Alliance prints no temperature range for alpha(Br) or beta(Hcj); ranges left null. mu_rec null. The 'about 0.65 T' mapping to BCN-19 is a choice (BCN-17 and BCN-29 listed as alternates).
SuperMagnetMan (library parts M5044, M5045, M5026): no datasheet with Br or Hcj was found; grade values come from K&J/Arnold as proxies.
Arnold N50M and N33AH are not in the 2021 Arnold catalog summary tables, so their Tw and three-decimal beta come only from the per-grade sheet (N33AH) or are absent (N50M Tw).
K&J publishes no temperature coefficients; Arnold's per-grade values are used for all NdFeB alpha and beta.

SmCo 'grade 26' and 'grade 30' are vendor-dependent names; Hcj min differs by sub-grade (Recoma 26: 1200, 26HE: 1500, Eclipse SmCo26: about 1512 kA/m). Arnold Recoma 26/30 selected; the user should confirm which sub-grade the calculator should represent.
